prompt:
Create one object as exactly SIX orthographic views in a single transparent atlas: columns FRONT, TOP, RIGHT, LEFT, BOTTOM, REAR, one row only. The sole object is the Personal Space NE timber-and-plaster wall segment in the source reference. Match the native image: warm orange-brown wood framing, pale cream plaster infill, a single dark-edged diagonal wooden brace rising diagonally across the plaster face, dark outlines, horizontal top/bottom timber caps. Do NOT use blue/gold palace stone, bricks, banners, or any unrelated architecture.

This is one long, upright wall whose long horizontal axis is world Y, thickness is world X, and height is world Z. FRONT and REAR look squarely at the narrow X/Z end faces: narrow wall thickness, full common Z height, visible timber cap/side frame and plaster edge; no long broad side. RIGHT and LEFT look squarely at the broad Y/Z wall faces: long horizontal span, same full Z height as FRONT/REAR, pale plaster panel, timber uprights and the native diagonal brace; opposite face can conservatively infer brace orientation but keep same construction. TOP looks straight down Z and shows a long thin rectangle along Y with only the narrow wood cap/edge surfaces, not a vertical wall face or brace. BOTTOM looks straight up and shows the matching long thin wood/beam underside footprint, no vertical panel. Keep equal object scale and height across the four elevations and coherent footprint between TOP/BOTTOM and side extents.

Each column contains one whole centered view with transparent margin. Keep cell silhouettes separate and unclipped. Crisp pixel art, no perspective/isometric, no text, no cell borders, no background/shadow.
